name: ACLU Foundation
mission: The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) Foundation is the arm of the ACLU that conducts litigation and communication efforts. The Foundation provides legal representation in cases involving issues of civil liberties and constitutional rights, ranging from administrative hearings to trials and appeals. In addition, the Foundation educates the public as to civil liberties and constitutional rights by disseminating literature and other publications. The ACLU Foundation preserves and promotes civil rights and liberties as guaranteed by the United States Constitution.
programs: Trone Center for Justice and Equality
theoryOfChange: The ACLU Foundation (ACLUF– our 501(c)(3) arm) seeks to defend and expand democracy and constitutional rights for all Americans, including: First Amendment rights, such as free speech, the right to protest, and freedom of religion; the freedom to vote and to have that vote counted; the rights of immigrants; LGBTQ equality; racial justice; and a woman’s right to determine whether and when to have a child. The ACLU also seeks to end mass incarceration and racism in the criminal legal system, including the death penalty, as well as discrimination against people with disabilities. Finally, the ACLUF holds the U.S. government accountable to the rule of law and universal human rights principles.

strengths_deep_dive: The ACLU Foundation displays strong institutional governance and financial transparency. According to filed disclosures, the organization maintained a <cite id="1">Program expense ratio of 83.5%</cite> in FY2025, outperforming the <cite id="1">peer program ratio median of 72.7%</cite> and exceeding the <cite id="1">75% industry standard benchmark</cite> [1]. Its fundraising efficiency remains exceptional, expending <cite id="1">only $0.12 per $1 raised</cite> [1]. Independent evaluators reflect these operational standards, granting the charity a <cite id="1">100/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite> alongside Candid Platinum transparency recognition [1].
rich_narrative.summary: The ACLU Foundation defends individual rights and constitutional liberties across the United States through impact litigation, public education, and advocacy initiatives [3]. Founded in 1920, the organization has built a century-long legacy of civil rights defense, operating programs including the Center for Liberty and the State Supreme Court Initiative [3]. In FY2025, the charity reported <cite id="2">Total Revenue of $306,750,536</cite> to support its civil liberties litigation and public education efforts [2]. Overall spending remains structured around public-interest legal advocacy, maintaining <cite id="1">a perfect 100/100 overall rating from Charity Navigator</cite> [1]. However, revenue declined in the most recent fiscal year, dropping 8% from $201,181,635 in FY2023 to $185,146,988 in FY2024 [2]. Operating reserves also remain notably high, with total working capital covering over three years of operations [1]. While the organization delivers strong legal programming, its scope focuses on general constitutional advocacy rather than targeted Muslim community services [3].
